lede: Bitcoin is hovering near $67,500 on Saturday after another wave of leveraged liquidations, as near-certain Fed-hike pricing and 10-year Treasury yields around 5.15% weigh on risk assets. Forex and gold are closed: gold ended Friday slightly higher at $3,883 but posted a weekly loss of roughly 3.5%, while EUR/USD finished near 1.1023.

focus.text: Closed Friday +0.2% at $3,883 after dipping to $3,867; sits below its $3,891.6 Monday pivot. 5%+ yields cap rebounds; US retail sales (Tue) and FOMC minutes (Wed) are next.
Ended at 1.1023, near the day's low and below its 1.1039 pivot, after a fourth straight losing session. US retail sales on Tuesday is the week's first real test.

technicals.indicators: RSI(14) ≈ 34 on H4 · below 50-day (~4,154) and 100-day (~4,196) SMAs · MACD below zero
technicals.note: Gold keeps printing lower highs and lower lows since the 11 Nov high near 4,066; Friday's rebound from the 3,852 yearly low stalled around the 3,900 area.

technicals.indicators: Stochastic deeply oversold (≈6–14) · MACD below zero and its signal line · price on the lower Bollinger band
technicals.note: The pair extends a sequence of lower highs from the August reversal near 1.1700 and closed the week under the 1.1044 support flagged by analysts.

technicals.indicators: Below 20-day SMA (≈1.3358) · MACD below signal line and zero
technicals.note: Sterling shed almost three cents from last week's 1.35 high and is resting on the 1.32 handle, with October's lows near 1.3140 below.

technicals.indicators: Below 200-day MA (~73.1k) · testing 200-week MA (~67.8k) · Fear & Greed 20 · negative perp funding
technicals.note: Bitcoin lost $70,000 and is now testing its 200-week average; the August low near 64,100 is the next reference on the chart.
Ether closed below $2,000 for the first time since August and is probing the 1,850–1,930 support band.

news.text: US October PPI rose 0.3% m/m, a touch under forecasts, but the 6.5% annual rate is the highest since late 2022; markets price roughly 90% odds of a December hike.
The 10-year Treasury yield climbed about 27bp over the week to around 5.15%, its sharpest weekly rise since April 2025.
S&P 500 slipped 0.4% to 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq 0.9% on Friday, yet both gained over 2% on the week; Nvidia lost about 13% after its CEO's exit.
Brent settled flat at $95.84, booking a second weekly decline as the IEA flags a surplus and Gulf flows pick up despite tanker attacks.
Gold logged a weekly drop of roughly 3.5%, its tenth loss in twelve weeks, while silver briefly slipped under $50.
Bitcoin sank toward $67,500, its weakest since August, and is testing the 200-week moving average near $67,750; sentiment gauges sit in extreme fear.
Roughly $1.7bn of crypto derivatives positions were liquidated in 24 hours per CoinMarketCap data, about $1.5bn of them leveraged longs.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $284m on 12 Nov per SoSoValue, a sixth straight outflow day led by BlackRock's IBIT (-$204m).
Ether ETFs shed about $524m between 5 and 11 Nov; ETH's daily RSI near 24 is the most oversold reading in months as price hugs $1,900.
Glassnode says stablecoin supply shrank $14.2bn in 30 days to 9 Nov, the steepest contraction since June 2022.
Solana fell 5.6% to about $76 and XRP slipped back below $1; Zcash holders begin voting on a treasury proposal from 16 Nov.

upcoming.note: Prev +0.3% q/q; feeds BoJ December hike debate.
Holder vote on removing 50,000 ZEC runs to 30 Nov.
Exp +0.2% m/m after +0.8%; control group exp +0.4%.
First report since the CEO's resignation; key for AI stocks and US indices.
Two dissents favoured a hike; watch appetite for faster tightening.
Media report trading could start Thursday; timing not officially confirmed.
